methodology: Sequential fresh native Windows GUI processes, no concurrent build/test; trace on, normal background drafts. Synthetic Qt inputs; completed QWidget paints, not compositor presentation. Active/exposed runs alone enter comparisons. All original samples, scopes and phase summaries retained; input phases retain CPU/thread samples and event counts. Timelines retain every changed-input >=100 ms tail and each phase's three slowest paints (20 ms margins). Nested Qt handler coverage is unioned, not summed; uncovered time includes other inputs, dispatcher/native work, logging and scheduling/waits. Coarse Windows CPU accounting and thread-state point samples are not exact scheduling durations. Cycle counts are not converted at an assumed CPU frequency. NtQuerySystemInformation is optional, absent in initial before runs. After comparisons use CPU/cycle sampling only, matching before. Scheduler diagnostics are a separate workload; their system-wide query cost is not attributed to editor processing. CPU fields in initial scheduler diagnostics were read before that query but timestamped after it; they cannot be treated as exact point-in-time CPU deltas. New probes record query duration and read CPU after the optional system query. WaitReason is meaningful only for state 5. State 1=ready, 2=running, 3=standby, 5=waiting. Zero-change inputs and shared/coalesced paints keep their original metrics. WPR CPU recording was blocked by local policy (0xc5585011), so there are no ETW ready-time/stack claims. Quantiles and clock differences checked from raw inputs. Working-set sampling is not heap accounting or a guaranteed peak.
